post.description:
Creates the product catalog of the connected Business account directly through the WhatsApp library, without the owner opening Catalog in the app first. It follows the official catalog flow: it reads the own catalog first and only creates one when WhatsApp answers that none exists (GraphQL 2498052), so calling it again is safe.
data.created is true when the catalog was created by this call and false when it already existed; data.catalog_id is the catalog id when WhatsApp returns it. Products can be created with POST /business/products right after.
Catalog operations need the account's business access token, which WhatsApp delivers to the session; when it is not delivered in time the call fails with 502 and can be retried.

get.description: Paginated catalog read, cached in-memory for 300s.

Uses the paired account identity and the official management query, like GET /business/catalog/own. Unlike GET /business/collections/{businessJID}, it lists collections still in review, rejected ones with reject_reason and can_appeal (for POST /business/collections/{collectionID}/appeal) and empty ones, and shows the current id of a collection after PUT /business/collections/{collectionID}, which may replace it. Does not change anything.
get.summary: Consultar coleções do catálogo próprio, incluindo em análise, recusadas e vazias

put.description: Edits a collection of the own catalog. The server versions the collection: a successful edit returns a NEW id (data.id) that must be used from then on; the previous id stops resolving (GET /business/collections/{businessJID}/{oldId} returns 502 with GraphQL 2498052). The edited collection goes through Meta review again.

Send an order message to a business. This allows you to send an order message to a business.
Optional create_order=true registers real catalog lines using each item price_amount1000 (integer thousandths), then sends the server-issued order. Default preserves legacy summary. Response order_created distinguishes both; a 502 with order_created=true must not be retried as a new order. When the registration itself fails (no order was created), the 502 keeps the error text and adds reason (whatsapp_rejected with WhatsApp's GraphQL whatsapp_code, timeout, canceled, disconnected, invalid_response, transport_failed or upstream_failed); no order, product or seller data is echoed.

post.description:
Creates a product in the own catalog of the connected session and returns it with its id.
price and sale_price are strings holding an integer in thousandths of the currency ("3000000" = R$ 3.000,00); currency (ISO-4217) is required with price and sale_price requires price.
image_urls (1-10, first is the main photo) must be HTTPS WhatsApp/Meta media URLs, normally the image_id returned by POST /business/products/image; other hosts are rejected by the WhatsApp library with 502 business operation failed (only the name, width/height and image count are validated with 400).
Country of origin is OPTIONAL in the API: send compliance_info.country_code_origin (ISO-3166 alpha-2) with optional importer_name/importer_address, or compliance_category COUNTRY_ORIGIN_EXEMPT without compliance_info when it does not apply. The official WhatsApp Web requires the choice for accounts with smb_product_country_of_origin_m1; omitting it is accepted by the server.
is_hidden=true creates the product already hidden. Products go through Meta review (status_info.status NO_REVIEW, PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED); hidden or unreviewed products are not exposed by public catalog reads (GraphQL 2498052).

Uploads one JPEG or PNG photo (image field in base64, up to 16 MiB) and returns data.image_id, the HTTPS media URL to use in image_urls of POST /business/products or PUT /business/products/{productID}. Send one call per photo and do not retry automatically after an uncertain failure (5xx): the upload may have been accepted.

put.description:
Edits a product of the own catalog. The PUT replaces product_info entirely: every omitted field is removed (for example, editing without sale_price removes the sale price and without compliance_info removes the country of origin). Read the product first with GET /business/catalog/own and send it complete.
price and sale_price are strings holding an integer in thousandths of the currency ("3000000" = R$ 3.000,00); currency (ISO-4217) is required with price and sale_price requires price.
image_urls (1-10, first is the main photo) must be HTTPS WhatsApp/Meta media URLs, normally the image_id returned by POST /business/products/image; other hosts are rejected by the WhatsApp library with 502 business operation failed (only the name, width/height and image count are validated with 400).
Country of origin is OPTIONAL in the API: send compliance_info.country_code_origin (ISO-3166 alpha-2) with optional importer_name/importer_address, or compliance_category COUNTRY_ORIGIN_EXEMPT without compliance_info when it does not apply. The official WhatsApp Web requires the choice for accounts with smb_product_country_of_origin_m1; omitting it is accepted by the server.
Products go through Meta review (status_info.status NO_REVIEW, PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED); hidden or unreviewed products are not exposed by public catalog reads (GraphQL 2498052). On read the server normalizes url with a trailing slash.

Returns the pack header (id/name/publisher/description/file-size/image-data-hash/tray image refs) plus the list of stickers (URL, direct-path, media key, file hashes, dimensions, MIME, emojis, accessibility label, handle). The response contains everything needed to download each sticker individually through /chat/downloadsticker — no extra round trips are required.

parameters.description: Sticker pack ID (32-char hex string published by WhatsApp)

post.description: Send an accept stanza for an inbound call. With the native calls engine on, a call the engine tracks is answered with POST /call/answer: this legacy accept does not connect the call (no media) and does not tell the engine.
Answer a ringing inbound call (manual mode). Returns 404 if the call is not found.

get.description: Return the per-instance native calls engine configuration. callProviderToken is never returned.
get.summary: Get the native calls engine configuration

put.description: Persist the native calls engine configuration. callRecord applies to the live engine immediately (the next answered call records or not; a running recording is not cut); every other field applies on the next reconnect. Empty callInboundMode defaults to webhook; invalid mode returns 400. callProviderToken is write-only: when omitted or null the stored token is kept; send an empty string to clear it.
put.summary: Update the native calls engine configuration

post.description: Originate an outbound native call. phone accepts E.164 digits (no +), a phone JID, or a @lid — anything carrying an explicit @ is used as given. A plain number is resolved to the callee's LID first, which is what makes a Brazilian mobile typed WITH the ninth digit work even though WhatsApp stores many of them without it. Set video to place a video call (H.264). Returns 502 if the peer is unreachable.

parameters.description: phone (string: number, phone JID or @lid) and optional video (bool)
parameters.name: data

post.description: Places an outbound group call to two or more targets. Each target may be a phone number, a phone JID or a @lid. WhatsApp rejects a group call with fewer than two remote participants. Pass groupJid to keep the call BOUND to a WhatsApp group while calling only some of its members — the only way to call a group larger than WhatsApp's connected-limit (32 including you), since /call/group/dial-by-id refuses those outright.

parameters.description: targets (string array, min 2), optional video (bool), optional groupJid (string) to bind the call to a group
parameters.name: data

post.description: Resolves an existing WhatsApp group's roster and calls every remote member. The call stays bound to the group.
post.summary: Place a group call by group JID

post.description: End a live call and tear down its media session. Returns 404 if the call is not found.

Legacy route. Returns 501 make_call_not_implemented by default; place outbound calls with POST /call/dial. When the instance sets GLOBAL_CALL_INITIATE_DIAL_ALIAS=true this route becomes an alias of /call/dial (phone and optional video; returns callId; requires calls_enabled and a connected session).

parameters.description: Only used when GLOBAL_CALL_INITIATE_DIAL_ALIAS=true: phone (string: number, phone JID or @lid) and optional video (bool)
parameters.name: data

post.description: Creates a reusable public call link. Anyone with the token or URL can join, subject to the waiting room.

get.description: Reads call-link metadata without joining. Accepts the bare token or a full call.whatsapp.com URL.

post.description: Invites one or more people to a live call. Returns the list of targets that failed, so a partial failure is visible instead of collapsing into one error.
Play an audio source (audioUrl or audioBase64; WAV/MP3/Ogg-Opus) to the peer. Audio is auto-detected and resampled to 16kHz mono.
post.summary: Play audio into a live call

post.description: Send a preaccept stanza for an inbound call. With the native calls engine on, the engine already sent its own preaccept when the offer arrived, and a call it tracks is answered with POST /call/answer: this legacy preaccept does not tell the engine.

Record the peer's audio to a WAV file in the instance's own S3 bucket. Mutually exclusive with the media stream per call. Requires callRecord enabled in PUT /call/config; otherwise returns 403 call_recording_disabled and nothing is recorded. Requires the instance's own S3 (enabled, with a bucket): the global S3 is never a recording destination. Without it the route answers 400 "voip: recording requires object storage (S3) to be configured" before anything is opened.

400.description: voip: recording requires object storage (S3) to be configured — the instance has no S3 of its own (the global S3 does not count)

403.description: call_recording_disabled: callRecord is off for this instance

post.description: Finalize the recording, store the WAV in the instance's S3 bucket, and return its object key (calls/{instance id}/{recording id}.wav, not a URL) as mediaKey (empty when no recording was active). On upload failure returns 400; the recording stays pending and is completed in the background, announced by the CallRecordingReady webhook with the same key.

Reject an incoming call. Optionally send a follow-up text message. With the native calls engine on and tracking call_id, the engine ends the call (reject while an inbound call is still ringing, hangup otherwise): the stanza goes to the exact device that called and the engine drops the call too. Without the engine, or for a call it does not track, the legacy reject stanza is sent unchanged, addressed to call_from (to its device when call_from carries one). The response body is the same on both paths.

Send a custom call rejection message to a WhatsApp user or group. This is NOT the same as /call/reject, which rejects the call itself — this one delivers a message alongside the rejection. With the native calls engine on and tracking call_id, the engine ends the call (reject while an inbound call is still ringing, hangup otherwise): the stanza goes to the exact device that called and the engine drops the call too. Without the engine, or for a call it does not track, the legacy reject stanza is sent unchanged, addressed to call_from (to its device when call_from carries one).
post.summary: Send a custom call rejection message

get.description: List the native calls engine's currently tracked calls for the instance.

post.description: Send a terminate stanza. Default reason is "hangup". With the native calls engine on and tracking call_id, the engine hangs up instead: its terminate goes to the exact device of the peer and the engine drops the call too. An inbound call the engine still has ringing is rejected instead (a callee that has not answered can only decline; a reject carries no reason). A reason set in the request goes on the engine's terminate as on the legacy stanza; without one the engine's terminate carries no reason attribute. The response body is the same on every path (action terminated, reason echoed, "hangup" by default). Without the engine, or for a call it does not track, the legacy terminate stanza is sent unchanged, addressed to call_from (to its device when call_from carries one).
Starts or stops sending local video on a live call. Frames are still pushed through the /call/{call_id}/video/stream websocket.
Turns the waiting room on or off for a call link. Admin only.

get.description: Server-Sent Events for everything peers do during a call: reactions, hand raise, mute state, screen share, group roster changes, waiting-room requests and call phase. Reactions are transient and cannot be polled, which is why this is a stream. Auth via ?token={TOKEN}.
Returns the authoritative participant roster for a live group call.

Upgrade to a WebSocket bridging raw PCM. Server sends binary s16le 16kHz mono frames (960 samples/1920 bytes per 60ms) of the peer audio; client sends s16le frames played to the peer. Mutually exclusive with recording per call.
Server-Sent Events stream for peer video state changes. Events are JSON objects with active, upgrade, orientation and raw fields.

Per-call video statistics while the call is running: participants sending video, frames received/delivered/shed, backlog bytes, and outbound frame counters. Use it to tell whether video lag is server-side backpressure or client-side decoding.
get.summary: Live video telemetry for a call

get.description: Upgrade to a WebSocket bridging raw H.264 Annex-B access units. Server sends peer video as binary frames; client sends binary frames that are forwarded to the peer. Pass fmt=participant to receive per-participant framed frames plus JSON control events (required for group video). Auth via ?token={TOKEN}.

parameters.description: Inbound framing: 'participant' for per-participant demux (group video). Default is bare access units.
parameters.name: fmt

get.description: Returns the pending-approval roster for a call link.

post.description: Archive or unarchive a chat to hide it from the main chat list. Archived chats are moved to the "Archived" folder and will reappear in the main list when a new message is received. You can optionally specify the last message information for proper synchronization. Set archive to true to archive or false to unarchive.

Delete a message from a chat (revoke — "This message was deleted" for every participant). Deletes your own messages in any chat. In GROUPS, a group admin can also delete OTHER participants' messages by passing the optional Sender field (the original author's JID, e.g. "5521999999999@s.whatsapp.net" or "123456@lid") — mirroring WhatsApp's admin delete-for-everyone. There may be a time limit for deletion depending on WhatsApp's policies.

Delete a chat entirely from the chat list. This is different from clearing chat history - it removes the chat from your chat list completely. The chat will reappear if you receive a new message from this contact. Optionally provide the last message details for more precise deletion. The delete_media parameter controls whether associated media files are also deleted (defaults to true). People are addressed by LID when known (index and last message key), groups by their JID. last_system_message_timestamp (optional, Unix seconds) marks the last system notice to delete (for example disappearing-messages notices); it defaults to last_message_timestamp, or to now when neither is sent.

Download an audio file from a WhatsApp message and return it as base64 encoded data URL. You need to provide the media information from the received message including URL, media key, and file hashes. The audio is decrypted and returned as a data URL that can be directly used in HTML audio tags or saved to disk. Supports voice messages, audio files (MP3, M4A, OGG), and PTT (push-to-talk) messages.

Download a document from a WhatsApp message and return it as base64 encoded data URL. You need to provide the media information from the received message including URL, media key, and file hashes. The document is decrypted and returned as a data URL that can be directly used or saved to disk. Supports all document types including PDF, DOC, XLS, PPT, ZIP, etc.

Download an image from a WhatsApp message and return it as base64 encoded data URL. You need to provide the media information from the received message including URL, media key, and file hashes. The image is decrypted and returned as a data URL that can be directly used in HTML img tags or saved to disk.

Download a sticker from a WhatsApp message and return it as base64 encoded data URL. You need to provide the media information from the received message including URL, media key, and file hashes. The sticker is decrypted and returned as a data URL (usually WebP format) that can be used directly or converted to other formats. Animated stickers are also supported.

Download a video from a WhatsApp message and return it as base64 encoded data URL. You need to provide the media information from the received message including URL, media key, and file hashes. The video is decrypted and returned as a data URL that can be directly used in HTML video tags or saved to disk. Supports MP4, AVI, MOV, and other video formats.

Adds or removes one chat (contact or group) from the Favorites list of the official apps. WhatsApp syncs Favorites as ONE complete ordered list (favorites app state action), so the gateway must know the current list to change a single entry: it uses the list last observed from app state or sent through this API (see GET /chat/favorites). When the list is unknown the request fails with 409 instead of silently wiping the other favorites; set force=true with favorite=true to replace the whole list with only this chat, or use PUT /chat/favorites with the complete list. People are addressed by LID when known.
post.summary: Add or remove a chat from Favorites

get.description: Returns the Favorites list. With refresh=true the gateway runs a full sync of the regular_high app state collection and rebuilds the list from the decrypted snapshot; complete=true is only returned after such a successful sync. Without it the list is the one last observed from app state or sent through this API; known=false means none was seen yet, in which case favorites is empty and does NOT mean the phone has no favorites. The full sync does not emit favorites events to webhooks.

parameters.description: Run a full sync of the regular_high collection first
parameters.name: refresh

500.description: No session or not logged in

501.description: Bundled library cannot return the snapshot

put.description: Replaces the complete ordered Favorites list with the given chats. This mirrors the official sync action, which always carries the whole list: chats missing from the request are removed from Favorites. An empty list clears Favorites. People are addressed by LID when known.

post.description: Mark one or more messages as read in a specific chat. This removes the unread badge and sends read receipts to the sender (if enabled in privacy settings). You must provide the chat JID, message IDs to mark as read, and optionally the sender JID for group messages. The operation updates the chat's unread count and last read message.

Mute or unmute notifications for a specific chat. When muted, you won't receive notifications for new messages in that chat. You can mute for 8 hours, 1 week, or always (until manually unmuted). Set mute to true with a duration to mute, or false to unmute. If no duration is specified when muting, it defaults to "always".

Pin or unpin a chat to keep it at the top of the chat list. Pinned chats appear at the top of the chat list for easy access. You can have up to 3 pinned chats on WhatsApp. Set pin to true to pin the chat or false to unpin it.

Sends the official PinInChatMessage (PIN_FOR_ALL / UNPIN_FOR_ALL) that shows the pinned-message banner at the top of the conversation for every participant. duration_seconds accepts 86400 (24 hours), 604800 (7 days, default) or 2592000 (30 days) and is ignored when unpinning. from_me tells whether the target message was sent by this account; for someone else's message in a group, sender_jid is required. In groups WhatsApp may restrict pinning to admins depending on the group settings. People are addressed by LID when known so the embedded key matches the destination.
post.summary: Pin or unpin a message inside a chat

post.description: Set chat presence status to indicate typing, recording audio, or paused state. This shows the "typing..." or "recording audio..." indicator to the recipient. The presence automatically clears after a few seconds, so you may need to send it periodically during long operations.

Send a reaction emoji to a specific message. Use empty string or "remove" to remove a reaction. The reaction appears below the message for all participants. Common reactions include 👍, ❤️, 😂, 😮, 😢, 🙏. You must specify the message ID and whether it was sent by you (prefix with "me:") or received from others. With "sync_invite_share" it must be a group JID (@g.us, no device) or the request is refused with 400 before anything is read or written. post.description: Change the name, description, picture and allowed reactions of a channel. Only the fields present in the body travel to WhatsApp, which is how the official client leaves the others untouched: "description":"" and "picture":"" clear those fields, while leaving a field out keeps it. name cannot be cleared; its maximum length is left to WhatsApp, which is where the apps keep it, so a name the server refuses comes back as 502 rather than being cut here. picture accepts a base64 data URL or an HTTP(S) URL (JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP) and is converted to a JPEG of at most 640x640. reactions is all, basic, blocklist or none. Errors: 400 invalid input, 501 when the bundled library cannot edit channels, 502 when WhatsApp refuses the change (for example when the session is not an owner or admin of the channel), 504 when the change was sent but not confirmed (the connection dropped before WhatsApp answered, or its answer did not read) — the edit is never resent, so read the channel with /newsletter/info before retrying. A change that never left the gateway answers 503 whatsapp_not_connected when the connection was lost before it left (a session already disconnected when the request arrives gets the usual 500 client not connected), 501 unsupported_client_platform or 500 not_sent, all with sent false: retrying is safe.

What WhatsApp applied to the channel and why, in five groups: suspensions, suspensions in some countries (with the country codes), posts found to violate a policy (with the post's server ID), removed profile pictures, and enforcements on admin profiles. Each entry carries its category, when it was applied, the explanatory texts in the requested language, whether and how it may be appealed and the appeal form link. locale picks the language of those texts (a code such as en or pt-BR, default en). An enforcement from an INTELLECTUAL-PROPERTY complaint carries the complainant's name and e-mail address in ip_report: WhatsApp gives them to the channel owner on purpose, so the owner can contact them about the dispute, and the official apps show them to the owner in their own flow. An entry the server reports as appealed but without an appeal time is left out, as the official client does. available is false when WhatsApp answers without any enforcement data for the channel, which the official client treats as nothing to show rather than an error: the five groups then come back empty, and that does not mean the channel was checked and found clean. Errors: 400 invalid input, 501 when the bundled library cannot read it, 502 when WhatsApp refuses. On a client platform that cannot send MEX requests the read answers 501 unsupported_client_platform with sent false; retrying will not help.

post.description: List the followers of a channel, the admins included, each with its role. WhatsApp never lists the owner (seen live); the official app knows the owner from its own role in the channel metadata. So when this session owns the channel, the answer adds this session first as the owner row, with source "session" and session_owner_added true; it is counted in returned and not in summary. When the session is an admin, no owner row is added: the metadata names no other owner, and none is made up. WhatsApp requires the session to administer the channel. There is NO pagination: the official request carries only a count, capped at 5000, so this returns the first limit followers, and maybe_more only says the answer filled the limit — it is not a cursor. WHAT COMES BACK PER FOLLOWER DEPENDS ON WHETHER THE OFFICIAL APPS WOULD SHOW THEM. The apps show a follower when it administers the channel or when you have it in your address book, and hide every other follower completely. For a follower they would show, the row carries lid, role, display_name, phone_number, username, followed_at and admin_profile. For a follower they would hide, the row carries ONLY role, followed_at, in_contacts false and identity_shown false: no lid, no display name, no phone number, no username, nothing that identifies the person. The row is kept so you still learn the follower exists and when it started following. summary counts WhatsApp's answer, so with_server_phone and with_display_name describe what the server sent whether or not it was returned, while phone_returned counts what this answer actually carries. summary_only omits the followers array and returns the counts alone. On a client platform that cannot send MEX requests the read answers 501 unsupported_client_platform with sent false; retrying will not help.

post.description: The numbers the official insights screen shows to a channel's owner and admins: accounts reached, followers, follows and unfollows, never who they are. Leave metrics out for what the screen reads: UNIQUE_VISITORS_OVER_PERIOD, NET_FOLLOWS_OVER_PERIOD, UNIQUE_VISITOR_OVER_PERIOD_BY_ROLE, UNIQUE_VISITOR_OVER_PERIOD_BY_COUNTRY, FOLLOWERS_OVER_PERIOD, FOLLOWERS_OVER_PERIOD_BY_COUNTRY, FOLLOWS_PER_DAY and UNFOLLOWS_PER_DAY. Every period covers 30 days; the per-day metrics give up to 30 days, one value per day with its timestamp. Also available by name: the NEW_UNIQUE_VISITORS ones (the app hides them by default), and the _ALL_ and _CHANNEL_STATUS_ variants, which the app reads only for a channel with channel status insights. By role, the values are SUBSCRIBER (followers) and GUEST (non-followers). By country, a row with a value under 10, or with no country, is left out as the app leaves it out, and hidden_country_rows says how many; at most 10 countries are asked for. data_status is available when WhatsApp says the numbers are ready and missing otherwise; last_update_time is left out when WhatsApp does not say. INSIGHTS ARE A FEATURE WHATSAPP ENABLES PER ACCOUNT OR CHANNEL. Before asking, the route checks what the official app checks before it opens the insights panel: the session is the owner or an admin, and the channel has at least 100 followers, read from the channel metadata (also when the channel carries the INSIGHTS capability); when either fails it answers 409 insights_not_available with the specific reason and sent false: nothing was asked. When the channel cannot be read for that check, 502 roles_unreadable with sent false; retry is safe. When WhatsApp then answers 400, the feature is not enabled for this account or channel (the app needs channels_producer_insights_enabled or the channel's INSIGHTS capability): 409 not_enabled_for_account with sent true; retrying will not help. Repeated metrics are read once. Errors: 400 invalid input, 409 insights_not_available or not_enabled_for_account, 501 when the bundled library cannot read insights, 502 when WhatsApp refuses or the channel could not be read for the check. On a client platform that cannot send MEX requests the read answers 501 unsupported_client_platform with sent false; retrying will not help.

The label is sent once and never resent after a dropped connection: when WhatsApp does not confirm it (the connection drops before the answer, or the answer does not read or carries no id) the route answers 504, because the label may already be on the post. post.description: Mark newsletter messages as viewed. This allows you to mark newsletter messages as viewed. The receipt is the official one and counts in the newer views definition, which views_count reports when WhatsApp sends it; the legacy definition may not change.

Get reaction and view-count updates of channel posts. The official request always carries a cursor: send after (updates for posts newer than that server ID) or before (older than that server ID, exclusive). When neither is sent, the gateway reads the newest post and asks for the latest `count` posts (default 25). since (Unix seconds) optionally limits the updates to changes after that time. views_count is the newer views definition when WhatsApp sent it and the legacy one otherwise; view_counts lists the definitions WhatsApp sent.

Get messages of a newsletter. This allows you to get messages of a newsletter. views_count is the newer views definition when WhatsApp sent it and the legacy one otherwise, as the official apps show it when WhatsApp enabled the newer definition for the account (off by default); view_counts lists the definitions WhatsApp sent and is omitted when it sent none. A poll's votes per option take a few minutes to reflect a vote or its removal, in the official apps too; /newsletter/poll-voters updates first.
Mute/unmute notifications of a newsletter. This allows you to mute/unmute notifications of a newsletter.

What THIS session added to channel posts: its own reaction emoji and its own poll votes. It reports nothing about anybody else, which is the whole point of the official request behind it. Leave newsletter_jid out to ask for every channel at once; pass one to limit the answer to it. Poll votes come as the option hashes in hex, so they compare directly against the hashes of the poll options. A post with neither a reaction nor a vote is not listed. Errors: 400 invalid input, 501 when the bundled library cannot read it, 502 when WhatsApp refuses.

post.description: Pin one or more posts, named by the server_id that /newsletter/messages returns, and get back the channel's whole pinned set as WhatsApp reports it afterwards. Two limits are WhatsApp's: a post older than 30 days cannot be pinned, and once four pins are active, pinning another REPLACES THE OLDEST instead of being refused — so read the pinned set in the answer rather than assuming your pin was added. A pin also expires: each entry carries expires_at and active. Errors: 400 invalid input, 501 when the bundled library cannot pin, 502 when WhatsApp refuses (for example a post too old, or a session that does not administer the channel), 504 when the pin was sent but not confirmed (the connection dropped before WhatsApp answered, or its answer did not read) — it is never resent, so read /newsletter/pinned before retrying. A change that never left the gateway answers 503 whatsapp_not_connected when the connection was lost before it left (a session already disconnected when the request arrives gets the usual 500 client not connected), 501 unsupported_client_platform or 500 not_sent, all with sent false: retrying is safe.
post.summary: Pin posts of a channel you administer

post.description: The channel's pinned posts, in the same shape /newsletter/pin and /newsletter/unpin answer with: each entry carries the post's server_id, when the pin expires and whether it is still active. A pin is not permanent, so an expired entry may still be listed with active false. This is a read of its own and does not change the pinned set; a channel with nothing pinned answers an empty list. An entry without a positive expiry is not a pin and is left out, as the official client does. It uses the current channel metadata document, separately from /newsletter/info, which stays on the older one it is validated with. Errors: 400 invalid input, 501 when the bundled library cannot read it, 502 when WhatsApp refuses. On a client platform that cannot send MEX requests the read answers 501 unsupported_client_platform with sent false; retrying will not help.
post.summary: Read the pinned posts of a channel

post.description: Vote in a poll posted in a channel, as any follower does in the app; the owner and the admins can vote too. options are the chosen options, each written exactly as /newsletter/messages lists it in poll.options[].name; WhatsApp receives the SHA-256 of each name, returned here in vote_hashes_hex, the spelling /newsletter/my-reactions and /newsletter/poll-voters use. A new vote replaces the earlier one, and options [] removes it, as the app allows. The votes per option in poll take a few minutes to reflect a vote or its removal, in the official apps too (seen live: 2 to 3 minutes); /newsletter/poll-voters updates first, so read it to confirm a vote right away. Before sending, the gateway reads the post and checks what the app checks: 404 post_not_found when the channel has no such post, 409 not_a_poll when the post is not a poll, 409 option_not_in_poll for a name the poll does not list, 409 too_many_options for more than one option in a single-choice poll (selectable_options_count 1), and 409 poll_ended once voting has closed; nothing is sent then. A poll that takes two or more options per vote is not limited here, as the app does not limit it: the vote goes out and WhatsApp decides. The vote is sent ONCE: an unknown outcome answers 504 vote_outcome_unknown with sent true and must NOT be retried blindly — read /newsletter/my-reactions first. WhatsApp's refusal answers 502 whatsapp_refused with whatsapp_code. A session that is not connected, already when the request arrives or when the vote would go out, answers 503 whatsapp_not_connected with sent false: nothing was sent, so it can be repeated once the session reconnects. Errors: 400, 404, 409, 502, 503, 504; every error carries reason and sent.

Per poll option, the accounts WhatsApp reports as having voted for it and when, and how many it reported (returned). Options are keyed by vote_hash_hex, the same hex spelling /newsletter/my-reactions returns, so the two answers compare directly; leave vote_hash_hex out to ask for every option. WhatsApp identifies voters by LID only, with no name and no phone number. A voter is NAMED here only when the official apps would name it, which is when this session has it in its address book: the apps keep every voter but name only contacts, leaving the others unnamed, and this route does the same — a row for everyone reported, with lid, display_name and phone_number only for the named ones, and voted_at for all of them. returned counts what came back within limit, not the poll's votes, and maybe_more says the limit was filled. The default limit is 5000 with one option named and 100 otherwise; the official client asks five per option, which it can because it knows the poll's options. vote_hash_hex must be a 32-byte hash in hex (400 otherwise). Errors: 400 invalid input, 501 when the bundled library cannot read it, 502 when WhatsApp refuses. On a client platform that cannot send MEX requests the read answers 501 unsupported_client_platform with sent false; retrying will not help.
post.summary: List who voted in a channel post's poll

post.description: The responses THIS session sent to a question, the official "View your responses", at most 100 as WhatsApp returns them, each with whether an admin liked it. They carry no sender: they are yours. This is a read and is not checked against your role first; WhatsApp's not-authorized and not-allowed come back as 403 not_allowed. Errors: 400 invalid input, 403, 404 when the question does not exist, 429, 503 whatsapp_not_connected when the session is not connected (nothing was asked), 502 otherwise.

post.description: Delete, for everyone, a response THIS session sent, the official "Delete for everyone" of "Your responses". The gateway first reads your responses to the question and finds this response_server_id among them, which also proves the response is yours; when it is not there the answer is 404 response_not_found and nothing is sent. The deletion is sent ONCE: an unknown outcome answers 504 delete_outcome_unknown and must NOT be retried — read /newsletter/question/my-responses first. Errors: 400, 403/404/429 from the read (404 post_not_found when the question does not exist), 502, 504. A session that is not connected, already when the request arrives or when it would go out, answers 503 whatsapp_not_connected with sent false: nothing was sent, so it can be repeated once the session reconnects. Every error carries sent.
post.summary: Delete one of your own responses to a channel question

post.description: Post a reply in the channel that quotes the question and one response, the official "Reply" in the responses list: every follower sees the reply and the response's text, never who wrote the response. Before anything is sent the gateway checks your role (409 not_admin), reads the question post (404 post_not_found, 409 not_a_question) and looks the response up in WhatsApp's own list, newest first, so the quoted text is WhatsApp's and never the caller's. The lookup reads up to 5 pages of 1000 responses — one read of the channel metadata, one of the post and 1 to 5 of the responses, so 3 to 7 reads before the send; lookup_reads says how many pages it took. A response outside the 5000 most recent, or hidden, answers 404 response_not_found with sent false. The reply is text, or an image or a video with an optional caption, and is sent ONCE: an unknown outcome answers 504 reply_outcome_unknown and must NOT be retried — read /newsletter/messages first. Errors: 400, 403/404/429 from the lookup reads, 409, 501 (501 also with reason unsupported_client_platform and sent false when this session's client platform cannot send MEX requests, so the role read before the send fails), 502, 504. A session that is not connected, already when the request arrives or when it would go out, answers 503 whatsapp_not_connected with sent false: nothing was sent, so it can be repeated once the session reconnects. Every error carries sent.
post.summary: Reply publicly to one response to a channel question

post.description: Send a response to a question posted in a channel, the official "Respond". Only the channel's owner and admins see responses, with who sent them; other followers never do. The text is trimmed as the official field trims it and must then hold 1 to 256 characters, counted exactly as the official field counts them: a symbol each, so an accented letter, an emoji with its skin tone, a flag or a family emoji count as ONE (WhatsApp's WAStringz count, neither UTF-16 units nor bytes). A 200 means WhatsApp accepted the response, not that the owner will see it: when the channel blocked this person, WhatsApp still answers 200 and the response shows in /newsletter/question/my-responses, but the owner and the admins never receive it, and nothing tells the responder (seen live, as in the app). Before sending, the gateway checks that the session is not the owner or an admin — the official apps give them "View responses" instead — answering 409 admin_cannot_respond, and that the post is a question, answering 404 post_not_found or 409 not_a_question; nothing is sent then. WhatsApp limits how many responses one person sends to a question (5 in the official client); over it the answer is 429 response_limit_reached (WhatsApp's 419). The response is sent ONCE: an unknown outcome answers 504 respond_outcome_unknown and must NOT be retried — read /newsletter/question/my-responses first. Errors: 400, 404, 409, 429, 501 (501 also with reason unsupported_client_platform and sent false when this session's client platform cannot send MEX requests, so the role read before the send fails), 502, 504. A session that is not connected, already when the request arrives or when it would go out, answers 503 whatsapp_not_connected with sent false: nothing was sent, so it can be repeated once the session reconnects. Every error carries sent.

The official "Block responses from …": the person behind the response can no longer respond to any question on THIS channel ("This person won't be able to respond to any question on your channel"); the block is keyed by the channel and the response, never by a phone number, and they are not told. THE BLOCK IS SILENT, as in the app (seen live): a later response from that person still answers 200 to them and shows in their /newsletter/question/my-responses, but never reaches the owner's /newsletter/question/responses. Block a response that is still visible: on one already hidden, WhatsApp answered 404 in a live test (502 whatsapp_refused, sent true). Like the official apps, the response is then hidden (hide, default true); hidden is true only when that hide was confirmed; when that second step fails, or is sent and not confirmed, the answer is still 200 with hidden false and a warning, because the block did go through — hide it with /newsletter/question/response/state. Only the owner and the admins can (409 not_admin, nothing sent). Sent ONCE: an unknown outcome of the block answers 504 block_outcome_unknown and must NOT be retried. NOT AVAILABLE IN THE API: unblocking (the official clients have no command for it), and reporting this response to WhatsApp — the official "Report to WhatsApp" option of this screen sends the response itself to WhatsApp's spam-report system; the API reports a whole channel (/newsletter/report), not one message or response, and a live test would report a real account. Errors: 400, 409, 500 (also with reason not_sent and sent false when the change could not be prepared), 501 (also with reason unsupported_client_platform and sent false when this session's client platform cannot send the change), 502, 504. A session that is not connected, already when the request arrives or when it would go out, answers 503 whatsapp_not_connected with sent false: nothing was sent, so it can be repeated once the session reconnects. Every error carries sent.

post.description: One page of the responses to a question, as the channel's owner and admins read them, newest first. count is 1-1000 and defaults to the official page of 30; has_more is true when the page came full, and next_cursor goes back as cursor for the next page. filter is all, contacts (the responders WhatsApp knows as your contacts), replied or starred; search narrows by text and needs at least 3 characters. WHO SENT EACH RESPONSE, as the official apps show it ("Followers can't see who responded, but admins can."): an address-book contact of the session by the address-book name (display_name, name_source contact, in_contacts true), anyone else by the push name WhatsApp sent (display_name, name_source push_name), and the picture (picture_direct_path) for both. A responder without a push name comes with the picture only, or with nothing; no name is made up. NO RESPONSE EVER CARRIES A PHONE NUMBER OR A LID, for anyone, contacts included: the official responses row shows neither. Followers never see who responded: their own responses (/newsletter/question/my-responses) carry no sender, and a public reply quotes a response without its author. Every action on a response (like, star, hide, block, reply) works with response_server_id alone. This is a read and is not checked against your role first: WhatsApp answers, and its not-authorized and not-allowed come back as 403 not_allowed. Errors: 400 invalid input, 403 when WhatsApp does not let this session read the responses, 404 when the question does not exist, 429 when WhatsApp rate-limits, 503 whatsapp_not_connected when the session is not connected (nothing was asked), 502 otherwise.

post.description: Post a question to a channel the session owns or administers, the official "Create question": followers answer it privately, only the owner and the admins read who answered (/newsletter/question/responses), and an admin can answer one response publicly (/newsletter/question/reply). The question is text, or an image or a video with an optional caption, uploaded like /newsletter/send does; WhatsApp decides per account which of these question types are enabled and refuses the rest. The session's role is read first and a session that is neither owner nor admin gets 409 not_admin with nothing sent. The post is sent ONCE: a dropped connection, a timeout or an answer that does not read answers 504 question_outcome_unknown and must NOT be retried — read /newsletter/messages first. NOT AVAILABLE IN THE API, by design: an audio or round-video question (the official M2 types, gated per account by WhatsApp and absent from the web client's default), editing a question (the official apps refuse to edit one: WAWebMsgActionCapability.canEnterEditingFlow and canEditText return false for a question), a dedicated forward of a question (it is the ordinary message forward; send it with forward_info.is_forwarded on the /chat/send routes), and questions in channel status updates (the API has no channel status). Errors: 400 invalid input, 409 not_admin, 501 (reason unsupported_client_platform and sent false when this session's client platform cannot send MEX requests, so the role read before the send fails), 502 when WhatsApp refuses or the role or the upload fails, 504 when the outcome is unknown. A session that is not connected, already when the request arrives or when it would go out, answers 503 whatsapp_not_connected with sent false: nothing was sent, so it can be repeated once the session reconnects. Every error carries sent.

post.description: Send reaction to newsletter message. This allows you to send reaction to newsletter message.

Per reaction code, the accounts WhatsApp reports as having reacted to the post, and how many it reported (returned). WhatsApp identifies them by LID only: there is no name and no phone number in its answer. A sender is NAMED here only when the official apps would name it, which is when this session has it in its address book; the apps say it in words, "You can only view individual reactions from contacts," and drop the rest from the screen. This route keeps a row for every sender WhatsApp reported, counted in returned and in_contacts, and gives lid, display_name, phone_number and the picture path only for the named ones; the rest are rows with in_contacts false and identity_shown false and nothing that identifies the person. returned is NOT the reaction count: the official query takes no limit and the server decides how many senders it lists, so the per-emoji count of /newsletter/message-updates may be higher. Errors: 400 invalid input, 501 when the bundled library cannot read it, 502 when WhatsApp refuses. On a client platform that cannot send MEX requests the read answers 501 unsupported_client_platform with sent false; retrying will not help.

post.description: The channels WhatsApp recommends to this account, the channel suggestions of the apps. country_code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) is optional: the apps send the account's own country, this route does not guess it, so leave it out for no region or send it to match the app. limit is 1-20 and defaults to 20, what the official client asks for. The official query takes no cursor, so this is a single list without paging. Like the app, the route hides the channels this account already follows (read from the account's followed channels) and the suspended or geosuspended ones, and says how many it hid in hidden_subscribed and hidden_inactive; returned counts what is left, so it can be smaller than limit. Report a channel to WhatsApp, as the "Report channel" row of the channel's info screen does (spam flow newsletter_info_report). It reaches WhatsApp's moderation and cannot be undone. The route first reads the channel's name, which the report carries; if that read fails, it answers 502 and nothing is sent. ONE DIFFERENCE FROM THE APPS: the apps attach up to five of the channel's latest posts to the report as samples; this route sends NO post samples, only the report of the channel itself, so post_samples_sent is always 0. Following the channel is not changed: the apps offer to unfollow in the same dialog, which is /newsletter/unfollow here. The report is sent once and never resent: when the connection drops or WhatsApp does not answer in time, the route answers 504, because the report may already have been received. A refusal from WhatsApp (400, 403, 429 and so on) answers 502 with WhatsApp's code. Errors: 400 invalid input, 501 when the bundled library cannot report, 502 when the name cannot be read or WhatsApp refuses, 504 when the outcome is unknown. A report that never left the gateway answers 503 whatsapp_not_connected with sent false when the connection was lost before it left (a session already disconnected when the request arrives gets the usual 500 client not connected); retrying is safe. post.description: Make another admin the owner of a channel. THIS IS NOT REVERSIBLE by you once it succeeds, so every pre-condition the official client checks is checked HERE, against the channel's follower list, before anything is sent: the session must be the current owner, the target must not be the session itself, the target must already follow the channel, and its role there must be exactly admin — the official selection screen says it outright, "You can only transfer ownership to admins." Each failure answers 409 with a machine-readable reason (not_owner, target_not_admin) and nothing is sent. A target missing from the follower list answers 409 target_not_admin: that list did not show them as an admin, whether they follow as a subscriber (WhatsApp can leave a subscriber out, seen live) or do not follow; a target missing from a follower list that came back full (5000, the same list the official app checks) answers 409 target_not_in_follower_list instead, because its absence proves nothing; transfer_to_self answers 400. If the roles cannot be read the request is refused with 502 roles_unreadable rather than sent unchecked. EVERY error answer carries sent: false when the request never left the gateway, so retrying it is safe, and sent: true when it MAY have reached WhatsApp — a conservative bound — so the current role has to be read before anything else. A 502 whatsapp_refused is WhatsApp's answer to the only send there was: these mutations are never resent after a dropped connection, which surfaces as 504 instead. What the wording does not say: a successful transfer leaves you an ADMIN of the channel, not a subscriber. The official apps drop that remaining role in a second step; here that step is dismiss_self_as_admin, which defaults to false, because getting the admin role back needs a fresh admin invite from the new owner. When it is asked for and only that second step fails, the answer is still 200 with self_demoted false and a warning: the ownership did move, and retrying would not undo it. When that second step was sent and not confirmed, your_role is unknown and self_demoted is null: read the roles with /newsletter/admins. A transfer whose outcome is unknown — a timeout, a disconnection after sending, or an answer that does not confirm it — answers 504 transfer_outcome_unknown and must NOT be retried: read the role with /newsletter/admins and decide from there. A change that never left the gateway answers 503 whatsapp_not_connected when the connection was lost before it left (a session already disconnected when the request arrives gets the usual 500 client not connected), 501 unsupported_client_platform or 500 not_sent, all with sent false: retrying is safe.

refuses a name that is too long.

picture.description:

re-encoded as a JPEG of at most 640x640 before it is sent; the empty string removes
the current picture.

reactions.description: Which reactions followers may send: all, basic, blocklist or none (case-insensitive).

invite_code.description: Channel invite code. Omitted when WhatsApp returns none.

jid.description: JID of the edited channel, as WhatsApp returned it.

when WhatsApp returns none.

location_name.description: Optional place name, at most 256 characters.

status.description: Optional state the invitation is sent with, case-insensitive: ACTIVE (default), CANCELED, SUSPENDED or UNKNOWN. The webhook can also deliver DELETED, LEFT_EVENT or REMOVED_FROM_INVITE_LIST, which are refused when sending.

thumbnail_b64.description: Optional JPEG preview of the cover carried by the invitation, in base64, at most 100 KB.

name.description: Event name. Required; at most 100 characters after trimming.

address.description: Optional street address shown under the place name.

here or in its alias jid.

personal data at all.

first 5000 followers can be read.

True when this session owns the channel and was added first as the owner row (source

main.NewsletterFollowersSummary.description: Counts over every follower WhatsApp returned, whatever the identity rule hides.

by_role.description:
Followers per role, keyed by the role WhatsApp reported; a follower without a role
counts as unknown.

in_contacts.description: Followers in this session's address book.

phone_returned.description: Followers whose phone number this answer does return.

total.description:
Number of followers counted here: the entries WhatsApp returned minus the unreadable ones
the gateway drops.

with_server_phone.description: Followers WhatsApp sent a phone number for, whether or not this answer returns it.

hidden_country_rows.description: Country rows left out because they had no country or a value under 10, as the app leaves them out.

role.description: SUBSCRIBER or GUEST, for the metrics grouped by role.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds of the day, for the per-day metrics.

The channel JID: digits followed by @newsletter, without a device part. Required,
here or in its alias jid.

code.description: Contact QR code or https://wa.me/qr/ URL, 1-2048 bytes, no whitespace (required).

businessName.description: Optional business name stored on the device.

pub.description: Optional public key, base64; ignored because it is derived from priv.

jid.description: The JID of the user.

pushName.description: The notify / push name of the user.

whatsmeow.SharableEvent.description: An event with link as WhatsApp's events API returns it. Times are unix seconds, except last_updated_ts_usec in microseconds; a field the server did not send is left out.

call_link.description: Call link of the event (https://call.whatsapp.com/video/... or .../voice/...); absent when it has no call.

call_type.description: Kind of call the event links to: VIDEO or AUDIO; absent when it has no call.

call_waiting_room.description: True when the call link has a waiting room.

cover_image_handle.description: Handle of the cover image on WhatsApp's servers.

cover_image_url.description: Address of the cover image, when WhatsApp sends one.

cover_is_preset.description: True when the cover is one of WhatsApp's ready-made covers.

created_at.description: When the event was created, in unix seconds.

creator_lid.description: LID of the account that created the event.

description.example: Agenda and goals for the next quarter.

end_time.description: End, in unix seconds; absent when the event has none.

event_id.description: ID of the event, as WhatsApp numbers it.

last_updated_ts_usec.description: Last change of the event, in unix microseconds.

location.description: Place of the event, when it has one.

location_web_url.description: Web address of the place, when WhatsApp sends one.

max_additional_guests.description: How many extra guests each invitee may bring.

reminder_time.description: When guests are reminded, in unix seconds; absent when there is no reminder.

status.description: State as WhatsApp reports it, for example ACTIVE or CANCELED.

latitude.description: Latitude, when the place has coordinates.

longitude.description: Longitude, when the place has coordinates.

AdminAuth.description: Admin authentication token. Must match ZUCKZAPGO_ADMIN_TOKEN environment variable.
AdminAuth.name: Authorization

UserAuth.description: User authentication token. Can also be passed as query parameter.
